title: Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives
author: John C. Hull
why: The reference everyone starts with. Not deep, but complete — the vocabulary of the whole field in one place.

title: Option Volatility and Pricing
author: Sheldon Natenberg
why: How a floor trader thinks about options. Greeks as intuition rather than derivatives.

title: The Volatility Surface
author: Jim Gatheral
why: The surface as an object — stochastic vol, skew, term structure — in a book a practitioner can actually finish.

title: Stochastic Volatility Modeling
author: Lorenzo Bergomi
why: The hard version. Written by someone who ran an exotics desk; the chapters on the smile are the best there are.

title: Volatility Trading
author: Euan Sinclair
why: Realised vs implied, forecasting vol, and sizing — the P&L mechanics of actually trading it.

title: Trading and Exchanges
author: Larry Harris
why: Market microstructure for people who trade — who the participants are and why they behave as they do.

title: Trades, Quotes and Prices
author: Bouchaud, Bonart, Donier & Gould
why: The physics-department view of the order book. Price impact, square-root law, and why prices move at all.

title: Stochastic Calculus for Finance II
author: Steven Shreve
why: The continuous-time maths done properly — Itô, Girsanov, risk-neutral pricing — with proofs you can follow.

title: Problem-Solving Strategies
author: Arthur Engel
why: The olympiad bible. Invariants, colouring, extremal principle — every trick, with hundreds of problems each.

title: Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads
author: Evan Chen
why: The clearest olympiad geometry text ever written, by someone who was on the other side of the table at IMO.

title: Linear Algebra Done Right
author: Sheldon Axler
why: Linear algebra without determinants until the end. The way to actually understand operators.

title: Introduction to Probability
author: Joseph Blitzstein & Jessica Hwang
why: Stat 110 in book form. Probability as a way of thinking, with the free lectures alongside.

title: Mathematics in Lean
author: Jeremy Avigad & Patrick Massot
why: The on-ramp to formalising real mathematics in Lean 4 with mathlib. Do it end to end.

title: Theorem Proving in Lean 4
author: Avigad, de Moura, Kong & Ullrich
why: The language itself, before mathlib. Shorter than it looks.

title: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
author: Shai Shalev-Shwartz & Shai Ben-David
why: PAC learning, VC dimension, generalisation bounds. The theory floor, free from the authors.

title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
author: Kevin Murphy
why: The encyclopaedia. Not read cover to cover; consulted whenever a method needs to be understood properly.

title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
author: Andrej Karpathy
why: Backprop, then a GPT, written by hand in front of you. The fastest route to earned intuition.

title: Attention Is All You Need
author: Vaswani et al.
why: The architecture everything now runs on. Short; read it after building one.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
author: Richard Sutton & Andrew Barto
why: MDPs to policy gradients, free from the authors. The foundation the reasoning-model era stands on.

title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
author: OpenAI
why: From Sutton & Barto to PPO with working code. The practical bridge.

title: The Mathematics of Poker
author: Bill Chen & Jerrod Ankenman
why: Toy games solved by hand, building to real ones. Written by two quants; reads like it.

title: Applications of No-Limit Hold'em
author: Matthew Janda
why: Range construction and balanced play, spot by spot. The GTO baseline a cash-game player actually uses.

title: The Theory of Poker
author: David Sklansky
why: The Fundamental Theorem of Poker. Old, but the logic of exploitation starts here.

title: The Mental Game of Poker
author: Jared Tendler
why: Tilt, variance, and process over outcome. Applies word for word to a trading desk.

title: Fold, Call or Jam
author: Pravar Kataria
why: My own GTO trainer: equity solver, Nash push/fold ranges, six exploitable bots, a daily puzzle. Built to learn stage 1 and 2 by doing.

title: The Intelligent Investor
author: Benjamin Graham
why: Margin of safety and Mr Market. The temperament before the technique.

title: Damodaran on Valuation
author: Aswath Damodaran
why: The valuation spine. His NYU site gives away the lectures, spreadsheets and data for free.

title: Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies
author: McKinsey & Company
why: The practitioner's DCF, with the accounting adjustments nobody else spells out.

title: Expectations Investing
author: Michael Mauboussin & Alfred Rappaport
why: Reverse the DCF: what does the price already assume? The most options-trader-friendly way into fundamentals.

title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
author: J. L. Kelly Jr.
why: The Kelly criterion, in the original nine pages. Sizing is the whole game.

title: Fortune's Formula
author: William Poundstone
why: Kelly, Shannon, Thorp and the story of bet sizing. The narrative companion to the paper above.

title: OpenBB
author: OpenBB
why: Open-source financial data platform. My equity terminal is built on it; the right free substrate for Indian fundamentals.
